x: Proceedings commenced with the five miles race and Redman (Met.) took the lead followed by Len Fletcher. Later Hake (S.W.C.) came through, and in the latter stages of the race a great duel was fought out between Redman and Hake, the first named prevailing by a few yards.

The time of the winner was 9 mins. 43 secs., and considering the heavy going this was quite a sound performance. In the 3 Miles Walk we saw a fine performance by Len Fletcher who, off 20 yds., finished second to L.
The annual contest for the right to hold the "Murphy" Shield for the ensuing year attracted a fair field, including a past holder in Len Fletcher, and the holder, Don Brown.

Pope, Fletcher and Wright preferred to start comparatively slowly, and speed up as the race progressed. Churcher walked strongly throughout and dropping his opponents, won fairly easily from Bidgood and Bentley, who were to fight out the Police Long Distance Championship on the following Thursday.

Churcher, Fletcher, Green, Harley, Readman and Rickards, should be our team. Unfortunately, Fletcher was indisposed, Green was unable to turn out, and Rickards was also compelled to stand down at the last moment.

McMullen, Hyde, Pope, Scammell, Green, Fletcher and Holland were the most prominent. Our 'A' team packed in fine fashion to win the scratch team race (3,6,7,9).
Belgrave were third, 9[illegible] seconds in arrears, and T.V.H. (Standen) just held off a fast finishing Aldershot (Fletcher, 15:49) to take 4th place.

Bob looked as nervous as a kitten as he took over 9 seconds down on Fred Bell (TVH) and 27 seconds down on Fletcher (Aldershot). Bell attacked immediately and gained ground all the way round, with Bob desperately plugging away behind him.
